$comment: GROUND TRUTH — authored independently of the implementation, then verified against primary source.
Every expected verdict below was checked against the live corpus on corpusVerifiedAt BEFORE the
engine existed. Quotes that turned out to be absent were the ones we WANTED absent (misattribution,
fabrication) — two drafted quotes were found to be not-in-corpus and one was corrected, and that
correction is recorded in each entry's `verified` field rather than silently dropped.
corpus: Harvard Caselaw Access Project bulk static (static.case.law)

coverageBoundary.note: Any citation past a reporter's boundary is UNVERIFIABLE_COVERAGE, never FABRICATED.

precedenceRule: 1. If the quotation is FOUND in the cited case  -> VERIFIED (even at low OCR confidence).
2. If the quotation is FOUND in a different case -> MISATTRIBUTED (positive find wins).
3. If ABSENT and the cited case's OCR confidence < OCR_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR -> UNVERIFIABLE_LOW_CONFIDENCE.
4. If ABSENT and the citation is past the corpus boundary -> UNVERIFIABLE_COVERAGE.
5. If ABSENT, in coverage, confidence adequate -> FABRICATED.

expectations.why: Control: a true holding correctly cited. If this line does not come back VERIFIED the tool is broken.
expectations.quote: Separate educational facilities are inherently unequal.

verified.note: Found with a capital S. The lowercase form returns ABSENT — this single case is the whole reason the normalisation layer exists.

expectations.why: THE HERO LINE. A real, verbatim sentence attributed to the wrong case. Every competitor reports a bare failure here; we must report where it actually lives.
expectations.quote: Separate educational facilities are inherently unequal.

verified.note: Brown's holding is ABSENT from Plessy (verified directly). Plessy's OCR is 0.434, below the floor — but the MISATTRIBUTED verdict wins anyway, because rule 2 is a POSITIVE find. That ordering is deliberate: finding the sentence elsewhere is strong evidence, and the low-confidence gate exists only to prevent unsupported accusations.

expectations.why: An entirely invented citation. Must be FABRICATED, with a populated resolution log as the receipt.
expectations.quote: summary judgment is warranted only where the evidence is such that no reasonable jury could return a verdict for the nonmoving party

verified.noteTwoThings: (a) `us` has 572 volumes, so page 1234 of volume 999 cannot exist — a cheap structural check worth adding. (b) The quote is a PARAPHRASE of a real Anderson v. Liberty Lobby holding (477 U.S. 242, ocr 0.695) that our string check does NOT find in that case either. That is realistic: fabricated citations are typically attached to paraphrased-as-quoted text. Ground truth is FABRICATED because the CITATION is fabricated, not because the sentence is new.

expectations.why: The coverage boundary surfaced as a verdict. This case is real, famous, and POST-DATES the corpus. A tool that is not boundary-aware calls it invented.
expectations.quote: counsel bears a duty of candor to the tribunal that is independent of any duty owed to the client

verified.note: Mata v. Avianca is the real 2023 AI-sanctions case that motivated this product. CAP static stops at 2019-08-19 for f-supp-3d, so we CANNOT verify it. Reporting FABRICATED here would be the tool's worst possible failure — accusing the most important case in its own origin story. This fixture exists to make that failure impossible.

expectations.why: An absent quote attributed to a badly-OCR'd historical case. Must refuse to accuse.
expectations.quote: the Fourteenth Amendment is not confined to the correction of legislation that operates directly upon the colored race alone

verified.draftingCorrection: This sentence was drafted as a plausible Plessy quote and then CHECKED. It is NOT in the corpus (verified absent, both strict and loose forms). It was retained as the low-confidence fixture precisely because it is absent: absent + ocr 0.434 < floor 0.5 is the exact condition the gate exists for. Had it been present, it would now be a VERIFIED fixture instead.

expectations.why: Reserved: a citation whose case resolves but whose record carries no casebody text, so the quote can be neither confirmed nor denied.
expectations.note: NOT YET WIRED INTO THE BRIEF. We have not yet sourced a real case with a metadata record but an empty/absent casebody, and inventing one would defeat the purpose of independent ground truth. Phase 1 must find a genuine instance (probe `casebody` presence across a volume's cases) and add the paragraph to the brief at that point. Until then the corresponding test is registered with `it.todo` so the gap is visible in CI output rather than silently missing.

knownGaps: E6 has no sourced fixture yet (see above).
Only reporters us / f2d / f3d / f-supp / f-supp-2d / f-supp-3d were measured. The slug map in Phase 1 must confirm the rest empirically rather than assume the naming pattern.
Single-brief ground truth. A second brief (ideally a real sanitised filing) should be added in Phase 4 to reduce overfitting to these six lines.
